name: Plumpton Park Zoo
distance: About 25 minutes west of Newark on Telegraph Road, and over the Maryland line.
blurb: A small nonprofit zoo in Cecil County, close enough to Newark to be an easy morning. Giraffes, tigers, bears, wolves, zebras, macaws and tortoises, plus mini golf. Peacocks and chickens wander the paths rather than sitting behind wire.
season: 9am – 6pm daily from Memorial Day through Labor Day. 10am – 5pm the rest of the year, with last admission at 4pm.

admission.note: Adults $21.95, children 2–12 $15.95. Published by the zoo, read 8 August 2026. Prices outside the summer season aren't published.

onSite.label: Mini golf
onSite.note: There's a miniature golf course on site.

onSite.label: Loose birds
onSite.note: Peacocks and chickens have the run of the paths. Small children will meet one at eye level.

warnings: This is in Maryland, not Delaware. Everything else on this site is in-state.
The zoo publishes neither its hours nor its prices. Its own site says only "Open 7 Days a Week. Hours Vary Between Summer and Winter." Ring before you drive.

photos.alt: A peacock in full display, filling the frame with its fanned tail of eyed feathers, its blue neck and green crest turned slightly to one side.
photos.caption: A peacock mid-display on the path. Not in an enclosure — just standing there.

photos.alt: A white and buff speckled hen with a wild gray crest of feathers on its head, standing on bare dirt beside a wooden fence rail, with a hoofed animal's legs visible behind.
photos.caption: One of the loose hens, working the dirt by a fence rail. Hoofstock on the other side.

sources.label: Plumpton Park Zoo: official site
sources.note: The operator. Gives the Telegraph Road address, the phone number, 501(c)(3) nonprofit status, the species list including giraffes, tigers, bears, wolves, llamas, zebras, macaws, cockatoos, hawks, tortoises and snakes, a gift shop and miniature golf. States only "Open 7 Days a Week. Hours Vary Between Summer and Winter" and publishes no hours or admission prices.

sources.label: Plumpton Park Zoo: hours and admission
sources.note: Read 8 August 2026. Memorial Day to Labor Day, 9am to 6pm daily with last admission at 5pm; adults $21.95 and children 2–12 $15.95. This record previously said the zoo published neither, which was true when it was written and isn't now.

reports.what: Peacocks and chickens roam the paths loose. Photographed on site.

outstanding: Confirm whether the paths take a stroller or a wheelchair.
Confirm whether you can feed any of the animals, and what that costs.

name: Newlin Grist Mill
distance: About half an hour north of Wilmington up Route 202 and over the Pennsylvania line, near Glen Mills.
address: 219 South Cheyney Road, Glen Mills, PA 19342
blurb: A mill built in 1704 that still grinds with water, sitting in 160 acres of preserve with a stream, ponds and a mill race running through it. The grounds and the trails are free — the mill tour is the part you pay for, and the two are priced separately. Wooded creek walking rather than open park: shade, stone crossings and a lot of water.

admission.note: The grounds are free. The mill tour is $10 for adults and $6 for seniors and children 12 and under, with members and under-3s free. Both published by Newlin Grist Mill, read 8 August 2026.

onSite.label: Grounds are free, the tour isn't
onSite.note: Newlin says it makes "our 160-acre preserve free to those who come to enjoy it". The $10 buys the mill tour, not the gate. You can walk the trails all afternoon without paying anything.

onSite.label: Dogs on leash
onSite.note: Newlin publishes it directly: "Please pick up after your pets and make sure that all pets are on leashes." That's the operator's own wording, not a review site's.

onSite.label: Welcome Center has moved
onSite.note: The visitor center is shut for flood mitigation work. Information and admissions are running out of the Archive building instead, Tuesday to Sunday, 9am to 4pm. Read 8 August 2026 — this one is temporary by definition, so check before you rely on it.

onSite.label: Trails
onSite.note: Unpaved throughout. Newlin publishes a trail map but no mileage.

warnings: This is in Pennsylvania, not Delaware. Everything else on this site except Plumpton Park Zoo is in-state.
Newlin publishes no opening hours for the grounds. The 9am–4pm Tuesday-to-Sunday window is the temporary Welcome Center in the Archive building, which is not the same thing as when the gate is open.
The visitor center is closed for flood mitigation construction. A mill on a creek closes for high water, and this one is actively working on flooding — ring ahead after heavy rain.

photos.alt: A wide, shallow, clear stream running through heavy summer tree cover, with a line of flat stones forming a crossing from the near bank.
photos.caption: The stream at the stone crossing. No mill in this frame — this is the preserve part, which is the free part.

photos.alt: A small toad sitting motionless in wet leaf litter, its mottled brown and grey skin almost indistinguishable from the dead leaves around it.
photos.caption: A toad on the bank, about as visible as it gets. I'm not naming the species off one photograph — American and Fowler's toads both live here and this frame doesn't settle it.

sources.label: Newlin Grist Mill — the park
sources.note: 160 acres, free grounds, and the leashed-dogs rule.

sources.label: Newlin Grist Mill — visit
sources.note: Address, phone, and the temporary Welcome Center arrangement.

verifiedSource: Visited, and photographed on the visit. Prices, address and the dog rule read off Newlin's own site the same week.
outstanding: Grounds opening hours. Newlin doesn't publish them.

Fishing. There's a Fly Fishing Club in the site navigation, but the pages behind it 404 and nothing published says whether the creek is open to a casual angler, whether it's stocked, or what a Pennsylvania licence buys you here.
May a leashed dog come into the mill during a guided tour? Leashed dogs are allowed on the property; the tour isn't addressed.
